utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, only that. But it would depend on the Court's accepting my proposal and Defence counsel accepting my proposal. If I could make that -- I could set that proposal out in a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, General Milovanovic worked all day yesterday reviewing documents, but was unable to get through all of the documents. There are two more binders; I brought them here to court. What I propose is that I give these to the Court Officer, that Defence counsel check these binders to be satisfied that there's nothing in it other than the documents and the forms for General Milovanovic to fill out. General Milovanovic has agreed to review them over the weekend and that he return them through VWS to the Court Officer, who would then distribute the form that he filled out. And then on Wednesday I would have that translated and that would be my examination, just those documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and he would then do that without being assisted by anyone or not in the presence of anyone?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Assisted by no one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, by no one. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I perfectly agree with that, but I don't think we need to check -- I certainly don't need to check the file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you have an opportunity. If you don't need to do it, that's fine, I take it. Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we're fine as far as that's concerned. We're all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Milovanovic, Mr. Groome has quite some homework for you, from what I understand. You will be provided with the binder where you find a similar series of documents and a chart where you're invited to fill that in. I do understand that you have declared yourself available to do that. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're right. This is what I agreed on with the Prosecutor yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, when we will adjourn in one or two minutes from now, I will instruct you that you should not speak with anyone or communicate with anyone about your testimony, whether that is testimony you've given already or whether that is testimony still to be given next week. Now, I would similarly want to instruct you that if you do this job, you should do it just on your own, without consulting anyone, without allowing anyone to follow what you are doing. So it will be a lonely job for you to do, but these are my instructions, which, of course, are based on your willingness to assist the Court. And it's highly appreciated that you want to do it because it saves us time in court to go through all these documents and then to learn exactly what we'll learn if we look at your charts as you have -- as you have given your information in those columns. Therefore, you are excused for now. We would like to see you back on Wednesday, next week Wednesday, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon in this same courtroom, and I already gave you my instructions that you should not speak or communicate with anyone about your testimony. Since there seems to be no wish to inspect the materials, they can be given to the witness. Is it two binders or one binder?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's two binders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two binders.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: One with 14 documents, one with 40 documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Milovanovic, you may follow the Usher, who will then hand out to you the two binders.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a brief decision to be delivered which cannot wait until next week, but we have to turn into private session for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Madam Registrar. I thoroughly thank all those who have assisted us for going again beyond the time, and so that the public also knows I'm considering how to -- I could pay my debts towards you. We adjourn. The Defence is invited, if they have any further idea, now having heard the examination-in-chief and knowing what will follow on Wednesday, to inform the Chamber about any assessment, any estimate, on the time they would need for cross-examination. And we adjourn until Wednesday, the 28th of April, quarter past 2.00, in this same courtroom, II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 28th day of April, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.
